notes: Literature check ran in strict mode (7 counted queries); the baseline query was refused (BBOB query had 5 concept words; hyphenated words count separately) and the `benchmarks` command detected no benchmarks, so no baseline scout table could be made. The method-name filter refused any query containing 'learned quality diversity', making direct claim queries hard. SKILL.md orders the literature check after the reviewers draft their reports, but the claim IDs it needs come from R1's map, which I defined in Phase 0 to run searches; I ran them after the reports were mentally drafted but before writing them down, a minor ordering ambiguity. The author names were visible in the blinded text; I put them in the fingerprint for exclusion only and ignored identities in scoring. The script flagged DNS (the cited baseline) as 'high conceptual overlap', which the guidance does not clearly say how to treat when the match is the paper's own baseline. Rubric tension: pool-position bands vs Overall (R3 pool 66 maps to composite band 55-61 yet own composite 61.6). Single model context for all five reviewers, disclosed in review.md. Figures were unavailable, so Fig. 1/5/6 claims rest on captions and text.
